facts.text: North Lakeville’s name simply tells you its location—‘North’ for its position north of Lakeville, and ‘Lakeville’ for its lakeside roots.
Before Europeans arrived, the area that is now North Lakeville was part of the traditional lands of the Wampanoag people.
North Lakeville sits within Plymouth County, a region famous for being the site of the first English settlement in New England, Plymouth Colony.
The CDP is roughly bounded by the Middleboro‑Lakeville town line to the east, Assawompset Pond to the south, Precinct Street to the southwest, and Route 79 to the north.
North Lakeville is an unincorporated village that lies within the town limits of Lakeville in southeastern Massachusetts.
Although it has no major tourist sites, North Lakeville benefits from nearby cranberry bogs that are a key part of the region’s agricultural heritage.
